mutualCap.description: Whether the cap applies to both sides equally.

consequentialDamagesExcluded.title: Consequentialdamagesexcluded
consequentialDamagesExcluded.description: Whether consequential and indirect damages are excluded.

uncappedCarveouts.title: Uncappedcarveouts
uncappedCarveouts.description: Categories of liability that sit OUTSIDE the cap, for example indemnity or confidentiality breaches.

supercap.title: Supercap
supercap.description: A raised cap that applies to specific categories, when the contract sets one.
examples: Two times fees for data-security breaches

indemnityExposure.title: Indemnityexposure
indemnityExposure.description: What you are indemnifying the counterparty for.

insuranceRequired.title: Insurancerequired
insuranceRequired.description: Insurance the contract requires you to carry.

claimTimeBar.title: Claimtimebar
claimTimeBar.description: Any deadline for bringing a claim under the contract.
examples: Claims must be brought within 12 months.

ReviewLiabilityExposure.title: ReviewLiabilityExposure
ReviewLiabilityExposure.description:
How much the reviewer is on the hook for, in one panel.

Every field is nullable and stays nullable. This is assembled defensively
from LLM output about contract language that may not exist: a contract with
no liability clause has no cap, and `null` is the true answer rather than a
zero that reads as "capped at nothing".

tier.title: Tier
tier.description: Priority tier: 1 is must-have and covers deal breakers, 2 is should-have, 3 is nice-to-have.

items.title: Items
items.description: What to raise at this tier, in order.

ReviewNegotiationPriority.title: ReviewNegotiationPriority
ReviewNegotiationPriority.description: One tier of the negotiation plan: what to raise first, and what to trade.

clauseName.title: Clausename
clauseName.description: Which clause this edit applies to.

sectionReference.title: Sectionreference
sectionReference.description: Where the clause sits in the contract, for example `8.2`.

currentLanguage.title: Currentlanguage
currentLanguage.description: The text to be replaced, as it stands in the contract. Empty for an insertion.
examples: Supplier's total liability shall be unlimited.

proposedLanguage.title: Proposedlanguage
proposedLanguage.description: The replacement text to send to the counterparty.
examples: Supplier's total liability shall not exceed the fees paid in the preceding twelve months.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Why this edit is being proposed. Suitable to put in a margin comment.
examples: Our standard position caps liability at fees paid in the preceding 12 months.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: How hard to push for this edit: `must_have`, `should_have` or `nice_to_have`.

fallbackPosition.title: Fallbackposition
fallbackPosition.description: What to retreat to if this edit is rejected, taken from the playbook's fallback ladder.
examples: Two times fees paid in the preceding twelve months.

grounding.title: Grounding
grounding.description: Whether `currentLanguage` was found verbatim in the contract. `verified` means it was. `unverified` means it was NOT, so the edit may be misanchored. `insertion` means there is nothing to anchor because the clause is missing. An integration applying redlines automatically must stop and ask a human on `unverified`.

approvalLevel.title: Approvallevel
approvalLevel.description: Sign-off this edit needs before it goes out: `none`, `manager`, `partner` or `gc`.

isDealBreaker.title: Isdealbreaker
isDealBreaker.description: True when the clause this edit addresses is at or below the walk-away floor.

nature.title: Nature
nature.description: `substantive` or `housekeeping`. Absent means unclassified, on a review produced before the pipeline classified this. Absent is NOT the same as `housekeeping`.

ReviewRedline.title: ReviewRedline
ReviewRedline.description: One proposed edit, ready to send to counterparty counsel.

sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl
sourceUrl.description: The page the neighbours were found for.

SimilarDocuments.title: SimilarDocuments
SimilarDocuments.description: Pages similar to the one asked about.

url.title: Url
url.description: The page to find neighbours of.

SimilarRequest.title: SimilarRequest
SimilarRequest.description:
Find pages similar to one you already have.

The URL is handed to the search provider, which does the fetching, so this
is not a request-forgery primitive against our own network. **If anyone ever
replaces that call with a direct fetch, this URL becomes attacker-controlled
input to our egress and needs an allowlist.** `HttpUrl` is what rejects a
non-HTTP scheme today; do not widen it to `str`.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: The value to send as `skillSlug` on an ask.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the skill is for.
examples: Master services agreement with Acme for the 2026 platform rollout.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: `system` for one of ours, `organization` for one your organization authored. Personal skills are never listed here.

category.title: Category
category.description: Grouping label, where the skill has one.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction the skill was written for, where it is scoped to one.

Skill.title: Skill
Skill.description:
A named prompt a question can be asked through.

Read-only on this API. Skill authoring is a product surface with an upload
parser behind it, and publishing a write here would make this API a second
authoring path for prompts that steer every future answer.

label.title: Label
label.description: The bracketed marker this citation carries within its section, numbered from 1 per section. Two sections both start at [1].

documentId.title: Documentid
documentId.description: The `doc_` document this passage came from.

documentName.title: Documentname
documentName.description: The document's filename when the summary was generated.

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: The verbatim passage. Locate this string in the document's text to resolve the citation; there is no offset to trust.
examples: in no event shall either party be liable for indirect damages

pageStart.title: Pagestart
pageStart.description: First page the quote appears on.

pageEnd.title: Pageend
pageEnd.description: Last page the quote appears on.

sourceAvailable.title: Sourceavailable
sourceAvailable.description: False when the cited document has since been removed from the workspace. The quote is a snapshot and stays accurate; there is simply nothing left to open.

SummaryCitation.title: SummaryCitation
SummaryCitation.description: One passage behind a claim, snapshotted when the summary was generated.

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable within this summary.

text.title: Text
examples: Neither party shall be liable for indirect or consequential damages.

claimType.title: Claimtype
claimType.description: What kind of assertion this is, for example `general` or `event`. Publisher-controlled and open: read it, do not switch on a closed list.

eventDate.title: Eventdate
eventDate.description: The date the claim is about, when it names one.

SummaryClaim.title: SummaryClaim
SummaryClaim.description: One assertion inside a section, with the passages that support it.

title.title: Title
title.description: Heading for this part of the summary.

content.title: Content
content.description: The summary text under this heading.

SummarySection.title: SummarySection
SummarySection.description:
One heading of the summary.

`content` is loose on purpose. `document_summaries.sections` is JSONB
written by a service this API does not own, and the shape has changed once
already; a closed model here would answer 500 for whoever owns the older
rows, which is the same reasoning that keeps every publisher-controlled
vocabulary on this surface a plain `str` outbound.

id.title: Id
id.description: Public identifier, `tpl_` followed by 32 hex characters. Name it when starting a run.

description.title: Description
description.description: Free-text description of what the template is for.
examples: Master services agreement with Acme for the 2026 platform rollout.

category.title: Category
category.description: The template's category, as the customer classified it on upload.

sourceFilename.title: Sourcefilename
sourceFilename.description: Filename of the document this template was created from. Published because it is how a person recognizes which template a run used, months later.

updatedAt.title: Updatedat
updatedAt.description: When the template was last modified (RFC 3339).

Template.title: Template
Template.description:
One uploaded template, as listed.

The TipTap body and the variable definitions are not published. The body is
the same editor document a draft carries, and the variable list is only
meaningful against it; what a headless caller needs is which template to
name and what came back after it ran.

title.title: Title
title.description: New display name. Defaults to the source title followed by " (copy)".

TemplateCopyRequest.title: TemplateCopyRequest
TemplateCopyRequest.description:
Copy a template, optionally under a new name.

Send `{}` to accept the defaults. A copy is a real second template with its
own id and its own variable rows, so editing it cannot touch the original,
which is what makes it the safe move before a lossy body replacement.

contentMarkdown.title: Contentmarkdown
contentMarkdown.description: The template body as markdown, placeholders included. Whitespace alone is refused: the converter answers it with a valid EMPTY document, which would be a template that renders a blank page.
examples:
# Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement

## 1. Confidential Information

Each party may disclose information that is confidential and proprietary to the other party.

description.title: Description
description.description: What this template is for, in your own words.
examples: Master services agreement with Acme for the 2026 platform rollout.

category.title: Category
category.description: How you classify this template. Defaults to `custom`; free-form, not a drafting category.

TemplateCreateRequest.title: TemplateCreateRequest
TemplateCreateRequest.description:
Author a template from markdown you supply.

**Variables are detected for you, on this call, and the response carries
what was found.** A placeholder written as `[COUNTERPARTY NAME]`,
`{{party_a}}` or a run of underscores survives the markdown round trip as
literal characters, and the detector re-derives the mark from it, so a
template authored here cannot land in the state where it runs and
interpolates nothing.

Detection is regex over the flattened text: deterministic, free and
sub-millisecond. The product also has an LLM refinement pass and this API
does not run it, so a template imported here may detect fewer variables than
the same file imported in the browser. It refines display NAMES and adds
spans the regex missed; the identifiers `slotOverrides` is keyed by are
deliberately left alone by it either way.

id.title: Id
id.description: Public identifier, `tpl_` followed by 32 hex characters. Name it when starting a run.

description.title: Description
description.description: Free-text description of what the template is for.
examples: Master services agreement with Acme for the 2026 platform rollout.

category.title: Category
category.description: The template's category, as the customer classified it on upload.

sourceFilename.title: Sourcefilename
sourceFilename.description: Filename of the document this template was created from. Published because it is how a person recognizes which template a run used, months later.

updatedAt.title: Updatedat
updatedAt.description: When the template was last modified (RFC 3339).

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Every fillable span, in document order. The `id` of each is what `slotOverrides` on a run is keyed by.

sections.title: Sections
sections.description: The template body, section by section, with the placeholder text left in place. Send a replacement as `contentMarkdown`.

TemplateDetail.title: TemplateDetail
TemplateDetail.description:
One template with everything needed to run it without guessing.

`variables` is the reason this model exists at all, and `sections` is here
for the same reason a draft publishes them: a caller deciding WHICH template
to run needs to read what it says, and the editor's own document model does
not cross this boundary in either direction.

documentId.title: Documentid
documentId.description: `doc_` identifier of a document in this organization to build the template from.

title.title: Title
title.description: Display name. Defaults to the document's filename.

description.title: Description
description.description: What this template is for, in your own words.
examples: Master services agreement with Acme for the 2026 platform rollout.

category.title: Category
category.description: How you classify this template. Defaults to `custom`.

TemplateFromDocumentRequest.title: TemplateFromDocumentRequest
TemplateFromDocumentRequest.description:
Turn a document you already uploaded into a template.

Takes a `documentId` rather than a file. Bytes reach this API exactly one
way, through `uploads.initiate` and the presigned part PUTs, so there is one
media allowlist, one size ceiling and one answer to encryption at rest. The
cost is stated: importing a template is four calls rather than one, and the
source file stays as a document you own, can list, can download and can
delete, which is how "which contract did this come from" is answerable
months later.

**A DOCX-sourced template keeps its Word structure; a later
`templates.update` does not.** Replacing the body through this API replaces
it with what markdown can express, so duplicate first if the original
formatting matters.

id.title: Id
id.description: Public identifier of this run, `dtr_` followed by 32 hex characters.

templateId.title: Templateid
templateId.description: `tpl_` identifier of the template that was run.

matterId.title: Matterid
matterId.description: `mat_` identifier of the matter the run belongs to, when it belongs to one.

status.description: Run status, using the same five public values as an operation. The internal stages `planning` and `extracting` both read as `running`.

draftId.title: Draftid
draftId.description: `drf_` identifier of the draft the run produced. Null until the run has finished rendering one.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: The prompt this run was started with, echoed back.
examples: Two-year mutual NDA with Acme Corporation, governed by California law.

slots.title: Slots
slots.description: Every template variable and the value the run put in it, including where each value came from.

completedAt.title: Completedat
completedAt.description: When the run reached a terminal status (RFC 3339).

TemplateRun.title: TemplateRun
TemplateRun.description: One invocation, and what it produced.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: Free text the extractor reads variable values out of. Optional: a template whose every variable is supplied in `slotOverrides` needs no prose.
examples: Two-year mutual NDA with Acme Corporation, governed by California law.

slotOverrides.title: Slotoverrides
slotOverrides.description: Values you already know, keyed by the variable's `varId`. Recorded with source `user`, and the extractor never overwrites them.

TemplateRunRequest.title: TemplateRunRequest
TemplateRunRequest.description:
What to fill the template with.

Context documents are deliberately absent in v1. The internal flow can take
document ids as extra evidence for the extractor, and the same route will
accept them additively; publishing them now would mean publishing an id
space and an ownership check for a feature nobody has asked this API for.
Generation from a prompt alone is supported by the pipeline as it stands.

id.title: Id
id.description: The variable's `varId` on the template, stable across every run of that template.

value.title: Value
value.description: What the run put in this slot. Null when nothing was supplied or extracted for it.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the value came from: `prompt`, `context`, `computed`, `user` or `default`. Read it before relying on a value: `user` was handed over, the rest were inferred by a model.

TemplateSlot.title: TemplateSlot
TemplateSlot.description: One variable and the value the run put in it.

contentMarkdown.title: Contentmarkdown
contentMarkdown.description: The COMPLETE new body as markdown. This replaces the whole template: a partial body is not something this format can express. Whitespace alone is refused.
examples:
# Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement

## 1. Confidential Information

Each party may disclose information that is confidential and proprietary to the other party.

title.title: Title
title.description: New display name. Omit to leave it alone.

description.title: Description
description.description: New description. Omit to leave it alone.
examples: Master services agreement with Acme for the 2026 platform rollout.

TemplateUpdateRequest.title: TemplateUpdateRequest
TemplateUpdateRequest.description:
Replace a template's body, and optionally its title and description.

A PUT rather than a PATCH, matching `drafts.update`: `contentMarkdown` is
the WHOLE body, so sending one clause replaces the template with that
clause. Title and description are left alone when omitted.

Variables are re-detected from the new body and the frozen-text hash is
recomputed in the same write. That hash is the renderer's integrity baseline
over the non-variable segments, so leaving it stale would check the next run
against the body the template used to have.

**This is lossy against a DOCX-imported template.** The rich converter
preserves Word formatting that markdown cannot express, and replacing the
body through here discards it. Duplicate the template first if you want to
keep the original.

id.title: Id
id.description: The variable's `varId`, and the key to use in `slotOverrides` when you run this template. Stable across every run.

name.title: Name
name.description: The detected or authored name for this variable.

label.title: Label
label.description: Display label, when one was set. Falls back to `name`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What sort of value belongs here: `party`, `date`, `money`, `jurisdiction`, `address`, `number`, `duration`, `text`, `other`. Drives how the extractor is constrained when it fills the slot.

hint.title: Hint
hint.description: Guidance the extractor was given for this variable.
examples: The counterparty's full legal entity name, as it appears on the signature block.

defaultValue.title: Defaultvalue
defaultValue.description: Value used when nothing is supplied or extracted.

position.title: Position
position.description: Where this variable sits in the template body, counting from zero.

TemplateVariable.title: TemplateVariable
TemplateVariable.description:
One fillable span the template declares.

Published because `slotOverrides` on a run is keyed by `id` and **nothing
else on this surface publishes one**. Before this model existed, the only
way to learn a template's keys was to run it once and read the slots back
off the finished run, which is a paid LLM call to discover a schema.

url.title: Url
url.description: Short-lived signed URL to download the report. Fetch it promptly and do not store it.

sizeBytes.title: Sizebytes
sizeBytes.description: Size of the exported file in bytes.

ToolReportExport.title: ToolReportExport
ToolReportExport.description:
A short-lived URL to the rendered report.

The route declares a response model and a PDF is not one, so the bytes live
in object storage and the customer fetches them directly.

format.title: Format
format.description: Format to render. `pdf` for something a person reads and forwards, `docx` for something an editor opens.

ToolReportExportRequest.title: ToolReportExportRequest
ToolReportExportRequest.description: Which format to render the finished analysis in.

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: Every part that was uploaded, each with the ETag storage returned for it. All parts must be listed; a missing one is not detected until assembly fails.

UploadCompleteRequest.title: UploadCompleteRequest
UploadCompleteRequest.description: Assemble the parts into the final object and start ingesting it.

mediaTypes.title: Mediatypes
mediaTypes.description: Every IANA media type this API will accept for an upload, sorted. Compare case-insensitively: media types are case-insensitive per RFC 2045, and this API folds both sides.

extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.description: Every filename extension this API will accept, sorted and lowercase, each including its leading dot.

maxBytes.title: Maxbytes
maxBytes.description: Largest single file this API will open a session for. A larger `sizeBytes` is refused at initiate, before any URL is signed.

minPartSizeBytes.title: Minpartsizebytes
minPartSizeBytes.description: The floor storage applies to every part EXCEPT the last. A one-part upload of any size is legal, which is why a small file is not a separate code path.

maxParts.title: Maxparts
maxParts.description: Most parts a single upload may be cut into. The part size is chosen server-side from the file size and returned on the session.

UploadFormats.title: UploadFormats
UploadFormats.description:
What this API will accept, and how it will cut it into parts.

Derived from `adapters/upload_media`, which is itself derived from
`app.core.file_validation`, rather than from the web app's
`get_supported_formats()`. That catalogue carries categories and security
risk levels and INCLUDES macro-enabled formats the upload path refuses, so
publishing it would tell a caller a `.docm` is supported and then answer 415
when they sent one.

`supportedMediaTypes` here is the same list `unsupported-media-type` carries
in its problem document, from the same constant. A test asserts the two are
equal, because the day they drift the error becomes the more accurate one
and this endpoint becomes the lie.

matterId.title: Matterid
matterId.description: `mat_` identifier of the matter to upload into. Must belong to your organization.

filename.title: Filename
filename.description: Filename to store, including its extension. Trimmed; whitespace alone is refused. This exact string is used to build the stored object, so it cannot be changed afterwards.

contentType.title: Contenttype
contentType.description: IANA media type of the file, for example `application/pdf`. Must be on the supported list or the request is refused before any URL is signed.

sizeBytes.title: Sizebytes
sizeBytes.description: Exact size of the file in bytes. Not advisory: it fixes the part size and part count for the life of the session, and a wrong value fails at complete time. Must be greater than zero.

folderId.title: Folderid
folderId.description: `fld_` identifier to file the document under on the way in. Saves a second call. Must belong to your organization.

handwritten.title: Handwritten
handwritten.description: Set true for scanned or handwritten pages to route the file through vision OCR instead of the text-layer reader. Leaving it false on a scanned exhibit ingests it badly.

UploadInitiateRequest.title: UploadInitiateRequest
UploadInitiateRequest.description:
Ask for somewhere to put a file.

`sizeBytes` is required and is not advisory: it decides the part size and
the part count, both of which are fixed for the life of the session. R2
cannot be asked to assemble parts it was not told to expect, so a size that
turns out to be wrong fails at complete time rather than corrupting a
document.

partNumber.title: Partnumber
partNumber.description: Which part this URL is for. Parts are numbered from 1 and must be uploaded under the number given here.

url.title: Url
url.description: Presigned URL to `PUT` this part's bytes to, directly to storage. No bytes pass through the Vaquill API. Keep the `ETag` the response returns.

expiresAt.title: Expiresat
expiresAt.description: When this part URL stops working (RFC 3339). Re-sign an expired part with `uploads.presignPart`; parts already uploaded stay valid.

UploadPartLink.title: UploadPartLink
UploadPartLink.description:
Where to PUT one part, and how long that stays true.

`expiresAt` is on every part rather than on the session, because a large
upload outlives a single signature: a client re-signs the parts it has not
finished through `uploads.presignPart` and keeps the ones it has.

uploadId.title: Uploadid
uploadId.description: Public identifier for this upload session, `upl_` followed by 32 hex characters. Use it to presign a part and to complete the upload.

partSize.title: Partsize
partSize.description: Size in bytes of every part except the last. Split the file on exactly this boundary or the assembled object will not match.

totalParts.title: Totalparts
totalParts.description: How many parts to upload. Always at least 1: a small file is a one-part upload rather than a separate code path.

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: One presigned URL per part, in order.

expiresAt.title: Expiresat
expiresAt.description: When the whole SESSION expires (RFC 3339), which is much later than any individual part URL. Past this, storage discards the parts and the upload has to start again.

UploadSession.title: UploadSession
UploadSession.description:
An open upload, and every URL needed to fill it.

Two things are deliberately not here.

The R2 object KEY. It is inside each presigned URL and cannot not be, since
an S3 presigned URL is a signed PATH. What is refused is publishing it as a
FIELD: a field is a stable, structured handle a client would build on and we
could never withdraw, whereas the URL is a fifteen-minute capability for one
object the caller was already granted. Nothing cross-tenant is disclosed
either way; the uuids in that path are the caller's own.

The DOCUMENT ID. There is no document until the bytes land, only an
intention to create one, and publishing an id for a row that may never be
filled invites a customer to store it and then poll something that never
starts. It arrives on the operation's `resource` at complete time, which is
the first moment it means anything.

uploadId.title: Uploadid
uploadId.description: Public identifier for the session, `upl_` followed by 32 hex characters.

matterId.title: Matterid
matterId.description: `mat_` identifier of the matter this upload is going into. Absent on older sessions.

filename.title: Filename
filename.description: Filename the session was opened for.

contentType.title: Contenttype
contentType.description: IANA media type the session was opened for.

sizeBytes.title: Sizebytes
sizeBytes.description: Exact size the session was planned against, in bytes.

totalParts.title: Totalparts
totalParts.description: How many parts this session expects.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the session is: `in_progress`, `completed` or `aborted`. Published as a plain string, so do not branch on it without a fallback.

expiresAt.title: Expiresat
expiresAt.description: When the session expires (RFC 3339). Past this, storage discards the parts and the upload has to start again.

UploadSummary.title: UploadSummary
UploadSummary.description:
One upload session as a LIST publishes it: no URLs, ever.

`UploadSession` carries a presigned URL per part, and a list that returned
it would mint `parts x page` signatures for sessions the caller is not
currently filling. A presigned URL IS the object key, since an S3 presigned
URL is a signed path, so a page of them is a page of capabilities handed out
for no reason. A caller resuming an upload signs the parts it still needs
through `uploads.presignPart`, which is the route that exists for it.

`status` is the raw `multipart_uploads.status` and NOT the five public
operation statuses. An upload session is not a job: it is a place to put
bytes, and it ends in `completed`, `aborted` or expiry rather than in
success or failure. The ingest that follows a completion is the job, and it
has an operation of its own.

UserSide.title: UserSide
UserSide.description:
Which side the reviewer represents.

Kept in sync with the FE `UserSide` union + `USER_SIDE_LABELS`
(`frontend/src/types/legal-tools.ts`) by the drift-guard in
`app/tests/unit/test_contract_type_taxonomy.py`. Request-only enum (no DB
CHECK), so widening it needs no migration; that guard also fails if a
`user_side` CHECK ever appears, because this sentence would then be wrong.

messageId.title: Messageid
messageId.description: `msg_` identifier of the message that was verified.

status.description: Where the verification got to. `succeeded` means the numbers below are final; before that they are zero.

overallStatus.title: Overallstatus
overallStatus.description: The headline verdict. `web_sources_only` is not a failure: the answer was built from web pages, which this verifier does not re-fetch. `no_claims` means nothing in the answer was checkable, which is the honest result for a clarifying question.

verificationScore.title: Verificationscore
verificationScore.description: Share of claims that came back verified, 0 to 1.

calibratedScore.title: Calibratedscore
calibratedScore.description: The same score adjusted for the model's known overconfidence. Prefer this one when you are thresholding.

totalClaims.title: Totalclaims
totalClaims.description: How many checkable claims were extracted.

verifiedClaims.title: Verifiedclaims
verifiedClaims.description: How many were supported by a source.

unverifiedClaims.title: Unverifiedclaims
unverifiedClaims.description: How many had no supporting source.

contradictedClaims.title: Contradictedclaims
contradictedClaims.description: How many a source actively contradicted.

claims.title: Claims
claims.description: The per-claim verdicts, in the order they appear.

verifiedAt.title: Verifiedat
verifiedAt.description: When the verification finished. Null while it is still running.

Verification.title: Verification
Verification.description:
Whether an answer accurately represented the sources it was built from.

RAG-NATIVE, and deliberately so: it checks the answer against the passages
that produced it, not against the open web. When a customer scopes a question
to its own documents, fact-checking the answer against the internet
contradicts what they asked for. The internal product has a web-backed
variant; publishing both would publish a choice this API has no way to
explain.

text.title: Text
text.description: The claim as it appears in the answer.
examples: Neither party shall be liable for indirect or consequential damages.

status.title: Status
status.description: `contradicted` is the one that matters: a source says something different. `unverified` means no source was found for it, which for a claim of general law is common and not by itself an error.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How sure the verifier is of this verdict, 0 to 1.

citationIndex.title: Citationindex
citationIndex.description: The `[N]` marker the claim itself cited, when it cited one.

explanation.title: Explanation
explanation.description: Why the verifier reached this verdict, in a sentence or two.
examples: Source [2] is section 8.1 of the agreement, which excludes indirect and consequential damages for both parties, so the claim is supported as written.

issue.title: Issue
issue.description: The specific problem, when there is one: a wrong number, a missing qualifier, a misattributed holding.
examples: The answer says the cap is eighteen months of fees; the cited clause says twelve.

VerifiedClaim.title: VerifiedClaim
VerifiedClaim.description: One statement pulled out of an answer, and whether the sources support it.

title.title: Title
title.description: Page title, where one was found.

text.title: Text
text.description: Extracted text, truncated by the provider.
examples: Neither party shall be liable for indirect or consequential damages.

summary.title: Summary
examples: Twelve substantive changes, seven of them in the liability and indemnity sections.

highlights.title: Highlights
highlights.description: Passages the provider judged most relevant.

publishedDate.title: Publisheddate
publishedDate.description: Publication date as the source reported it, unparsed.

authorityScore.title: Authorityscore
authorityScore.description: How authoritative the host is for legal content, 0 to 1. A property of the DOMAIN, not of our ranking.

isAuthoritativeSource.title: Isauthoritativesource
isAuthoritativeSource.description: Whether the host is a court, legislature or agency.

WebResult.title: WebResult
WebResult.description: One page a web search found.

query.title: Query
query.description: What to search for. Written as a search query rather than as a question; the provider is a search engine, not a model.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: How many results to return, 1 to 20.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Legal jurisdiction to steer the search toward.

WebSearchRequest.title: WebSearchRequest
WebSearchRequest.description: A one-off web search. Touches no client data and stores nothing.

WebSearchResults.title: WebSearchResults
WebSearchResults.description: What a web search returned. Nothing is stored.

key.title: Key
key.description: Slug identifying this artifact. Pass it to the artifact download route to get bytes.

contentType.title: Contenttype
contentType.description: IANA media type of the produced file.

sizeBytes.title: Sizebytes
sizeBytes.description: Size of the artifact in bytes, when known.

WorkflowArtifact.title: WorkflowArtifact
WorkflowArtifact.description:
An artifact a finished run produced. No URL: fetching one is its own call.

Separating the listing from the signing is what lets the download route
re-check the installation at signing time, so a URL cannot be minted for an
installation that was revoked between the two.

key.title: Key
key.description: The artifact that was signed for.

url.title: Url
url.description: Short-lived signed URL to download the artifact bytes. Fetch it promptly and do not store it.

WorkflowArtifactDownload.title: WorkflowArtifactDownload
WorkflowArtifactDownload.description: A short-lived pointer to one artifact's bytes.

key.title: Key
key.description: Stable slug for this artifact. This is the value `workflowRuns.artifact` takes, so a download can be wired up before anything is run.

contentType.title: Contenttype
contentType.description: IANA media type the artifact will be produced in.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the artifact contains.
examples: Master services agreement with Acme for the 2026 platform rollout.

WorkflowArtifactSpec.title: WorkflowArtifactSpec
WorkflowArtifactSpec.description:
A deliverable this workflow produces, named before it exists.

`key` is what `workflowRuns.artifact` takes, so a customer can wire up the
download before running anything. `sampleUrl` is not carried over: it points
into the web app's static tree and means nothing to a backend.

id.title: Id
id.description: Identifier of the workflow definition. Pass it in the path when launching a run.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the workflow does.
examples: Master services agreement with Acme for the 2026 platform rollout.

estimatedMinutesMin.title: Estimatedminutesmin
estimatedMinutesMin.description: Low end of the expected run time in minutes. Use it to size your polling interval.

estimatedMinutesMax.title: Estimatedminutesmax
estimatedMinutesMax.description: High end of the expected run time in minutes.

documentSlots.title: Documentslots
documentSlots.description: What documents the workflow accepts, and in which roles. Validate against this before launching rather than discovering the shape from 422s.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: The questions this workflow asks. Their `key` values are the keys of the run request's `inputs` object.

artifacts.title: Artifacts
artifacts.description: The deliverables a finished run produces.

bestFor.title: Bestfor
bestFor.description: When to reach for this workflow, in plain language.
examples: A first pass over a counterparty's standard form.

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.description: What this workflow does not do. Worth reading before wiring it into an automated path.

WorkflowDefinition.title: WorkflowDefinition
WorkflowDefinition.description:
One catalogue entry.

Only active definitions are listed. A retired one still resolves in code so
old runs stay readable, but offering it would be offering something the
launch route refuses.

role.title: Role
role.description: The role slug to pass as a document's `role` when launching a run.

description.title: Description
description.description: What sort of document belongs in this slot.
examples: Master services agreement with Acme for the 2026 platform rollout.

minCount.title: Mincount
minCount.description: Fewest documents accepted in this role.

maxCount.title: Maxcount
maxCount.description: Most documents accepted in this role.

required.title: Required
required.description: True when a run cannot start without at least one document in this role.

WorkflowDocumentSlot.title: WorkflowDocumentSlot
WorkflowDocumentSlot.description:
What a definition will accept in one role, so a caller can validate first.

Published because the alternative is a customer discovering the shape of a
workflow by submitting runs and reading 422s.

key.title: Key
key.description: The key to use for this field inside the run request's `inputs` object.

fieldType.title: Fieldtype
fieldType.description: What sort of value is expected, for example a string, a date or a choice. A plain string, since the internal vocabulary grows whenever the launcher gains a widget.

required.title: Required
required.description: True when a run is refused without this input.

options.title: Options
options.description: Allowed values when the field is a choice.

helpText.title: Helptext
helpText.description: Extra guidance on what to supply.
examples: The counterparty's full legal entity name.

WorkflowInputField.title: WorkflowInputField
WorkflowInputField.description: One question the definition asks, and how it is answered.

id.title: Id
id.description: Public identifier, `wfr_` followed by 32 hex characters.

matterId.title: Matterid
matterId.description: `mat_` identifier of the matter this run belongs to.

workflowId.title: Workflowid
workflowId.description: Identifier of the workflow definition that was run.

status.description: Run status, using the same five public values as an operation. The internal stage vocabulary (`preparing`, `extracting`, `synthesizing`, `rendering`) all reads as `running`.

progressPercent.title: Progresspercent
progressPercent.description: How far along the run is, 0 to 100. This is what carries progress, since the stages all collapse to `running`.

progressMessage.title: Progressmessage
progressMessage.description: Short human-readable stage label, for example 'synthesizing findings'. Free text for a progress line only. Never branch on it; branch on `status`.

artifacts.title: Artifacts
artifacts.description: Deliverables produced so far. Listing is separate from downloading, so that a URL cannot be minted for an installation revoked between the two calls.

completedAt.title: Completedat
completedAt.description: When the run reached a terminal status (RFC 3339).

updatedAt.title: Updatedat
updatedAt.description: When the run was last updated (RFC 3339).

WorkflowRun.title: WorkflowRun
WorkflowRun.description:
One run. `status` is the public five, never the stored spelling.

The internal vocabulary has eight values, five of which (`preparing`,
`extracting`, `synthesizing`, `rendering`, plus `pending`) describe a stage
rather than an outcome. Those read as `running`, and `progressPercent` is
what carries how far along it is.

documentId.title: Documentid
documentId.description: `doc_` identifier of the document to attach. Must be in this matter.

role.title: Role
role.description: What part this document plays in the run. Must be a role the definition declares in its `documentSlots`.

position.title: Position
position.description: Order within the role, counting from 0. Matters when a role accepts more than one document.

WorkflowRunDocument.title: WorkflowRunDocument
WorkflowRunDocument.description: One document attached to a run, in a role the definition declares.

title.title: Title
title.description: Display title for this run. Omit to take the definition's own title.

documents.title: Documents
documents.description: Documents to attach, each in a role the definition declares.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: Answers to the definition's questions, keyed by each input field's `key`. Untyped here because every definition declares its own field set; read `workflows.list` for the shape this workflow expects.

WorkflowRunRequest.title: WorkflowRunRequest
WorkflowRunRequest.description:
Launch a run of one definition inside one matter.

`inputs` is `dict[str, Any]` because each definition declares its own field
set, which `workflows.list` publishes and the definition itself validates.
Typing it here would mean generating one request model per workflow and
regenerating the OpenAPI document every time a definition gained a field.

There is no `countryCode`. Every active workflow is US-scoped after the 2026
pivot, and the internal route stopped accepting one for the same reason.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. Branch on `type`, which is stable; `title` and `detail` are written for people and may be reworded. Some problems carry extra members (`requiredScopes`, `limit`, `expectedVersion`), which is why this object is open.

type.description: The stable identifier for this error, and the one field to branch on. Resolves to a page describing it.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated.

detail.description: What went wrong on this specific request. May be reworded at any time.
examples: This credential carries matters:read. This operation needs matters:write.

instance.description: The path this problem occurred on.

requestId.description: The id of this request, identical to the `X-Request-ID` response header. Quote it when contacting support.

ValidationProblem.title: ValidationProblem
ValidationProblem.description: A problem document for a schema rejection. `errors` lists the fields that were refused. The value you submitted is deliberately not echoed, so a validation failure cannot copy your content into an error response or into either side's logs.

type.description: The stable identifier for this error, and the one field to branch on. Resolves to a page describing it.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated.

detail.description: What went wrong on this specific request. May be reworded at any time.
examples: This credential carries matters:read. This operation needs matters:write.

instance.description: The path this problem occurred on.

requestId.description: The id of this request, identical to the `X-Request-ID` response header. Quote it when contacting support.

location.description: Dotted path to the rejected field, for example `body.contentMarkdown`.

WorkspaceAuth.description: Workspace credential issued from the automation console at `/automation`. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer vq_ws_...`. This is NOT a Data API key: a `vq_key_` credential is refused here and names the other product in the error.

externalDocs.description: Getting started guide and error reference

tags.name: Operations
tags.description: The one job envelope. Every long-running call answers `202` with an operation, and polling this resource is the only way to learn it finished: there are no webhooks. Five statuses, no synonyms.

tags.name: Clients
tags.description: The people and companies matters are filed under. Synchronous CRUD.

tags.name: Matters
tags.description: The unit of work everything else hangs off. A matter scopes documents, drafts, reviews, comparisons and matrices, and it is what a credential's access is checked against.

tags.name: Folders
tags.description: Organization inside and across matters. The same folders the web app shows, so one created here appears in the customer's browser.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description: Files in a matter: their metadata, their ingested text, and the original bytes. A document is only usable by retrieval, drafting and review once its status is `succeeded`.

tags.name: Uploads
tags.description: Getting files in. One presigned multipart flow at every size, with the bytes going straight to storage and never through this API. Initiate, PUT each part, then complete.

tags.name: Research
tags.description: Asking legal questions and getting grounded, cited answers. This API does NOT stream: an ask answers `202` and you poll the operation, then read the answer off the message it points at. Conversation state is kept here, so you hold a chat id rather than replaying a transcript. Also covers the matter settings behind an answer, the skills you can ask through, and the standalone web-research tools.

tags.name: Drafting
tags.description: Generating, revising and exporting draft documents. Bodies come out as sections and go in as markdown; the editor's own format is never on the wire. Rendered files come from the export route.

tags.name: Playbooks
tags.description: The organization's negotiating positions, per contract type, and the starter templates to build them from. A playbook is the input a contract review is measured against.

tags.name: Reviews
tags.description: Reviewing one contract against a playbook: clause analysis, redlines, flags, liability exposure and a reported sign-off gate. Export applies the redlines as native Word tracked changes.

tags.name: Facts
tags.description: The cross-document fact ledger for a matter: what every document in it asserts, coalesced and cited back to its source passages.

tags.name: Matter summary
tags.description: A citation-backed summary of everything filed to a matter, generated on demand and readable claim by claim.

tags.name: Chronology
tags.description: The dated events across a matter's documents, as one timeline, with duplicate and date-conflict flags.

tags.name: NDA triage
tags.description: Screening one inbound NDA against ten standard criteria and, where you name one, your own NDA playbook. Answers `green`, `yellow` or `red` with the reasoning per criterion, plus a report you can forward.

tags.name: Compliance
tags.description: Checking one document against one regulation's requirement checklist: a verdict per requirement with the article it comes from, the gaps, and what to do about them. Only regulations with a real checklist behind them are accepted.

tags.name: Comparisons
tags.description: Diffing two documents in a matter into structural changes, with a substantive-versus-cosmetic judgment and a downloadable redline.

tags.name: Matrices
tags.description: Spreadsheet-style extraction across many documents: rows are documents, columns are questions, cells are answers with verified citations. Building a grid is free; running it is what costs.

tags.name: Workflows
tags.description: Multi-step analyses from a fixed catalogue. Read a definition to learn what documents and inputs it takes, launch a run inside a matter, then download the artifacts it produces.
